title: My sadaqah hands
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Spring 1: Islam and the five pillars
source: Written for islamic-studies/y1 lesson 13 (Pupil PDF worksheet: my sadaqah hands)
intro: Lesson 13: Zakah and sadaqah: giving to people in need. Listen, look, then do the tasks with a grown-up.

panels.title: Zakah: the third pillar
points: Muslims with enough money must give some
It goes to poor and needy people
Giving makes our money clean and blessed

panels.title: Sadaqah: everyone can give
points: Sadaqah is any good we give
Helping and kind words count too

cards: A grown-up gives part of their savings each year
Money given every year to the poor
I give my old coat to someone cold
blocks.title: Sort into: Zakah / Sadaqah
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Zakah, Sadaqah.
blocks.answer: Zakah: A grown-up gives part of their savings each year; Money given every year to the poor. Sadaqah: I share my lunch; I help Mum tidy up; I give my old coat to someone cold

box.title: Draw round both hands. On each finger, write or draw one way you can give sadaqah (a smile, sharing, helping, a coin, kind words).

keywords.def: money Muslims must give each year to people in need
any good thing we give or do to help
the visit to the Ka'bah in Makkah

questions.q: Say two kinds of sadaqah a child can give.
questions.a: For example: share food, help someone

questions.q: Fasting in Ramadan is the pillar called ...
Draw two hands giving. Write one way you will give sadaqah this week.
questions.a: For example: I will give my toy car to my cousin.

questions.q: Stretch: why does Allah love it when we give?
questions.a: It helps people and shows we care, and Allah rewards it.

questions.q: Which one can every child do?
questions.a: A) Give sadaqah. Sadaqah can be any good deed, so every child can give it.

questions.q: Think again: what would you do with the apple, and why?
questions.a: Share it, because Islam teaches us to give.
